sections.h2: Who bills property tax inside Columbia city limits?
sections.html:
A Columbia homeowner receives two obligations: one to the City of Columbia and one to Maury County. The city's Property Tax page says residents inside the corporate limits owe both.

The county's Property Assessor, Bobby Daniels, is at 6 Public Square, phone 931-375-4001, and sets values. Collection of the county portion belongs to the Trustee at 1 Public Square, phone 931-375-2201, open weekdays from 8 to 4.

County notices are addressed to whoever owned the parcel on January 1. A bill that never reaches you still carries interest once it goes delinquent, because state law does not require notices to be mailed.

sections.h2: When does Columbia city property tax come due, and is the window open now?
sections.html:
The city accepts payment without penalty from November 1 through December 15. As of today, November 15, 2026, that stretch is half over and one month remains.

Late charges stack up in three steps after the window closes:

  • A 0.5% charge applies through the end of December.
  • Another 0.5% accrues starting January 1.
  • From February 1, the city adds 1% for every month the balance stays open.

The City Recorder page repeats the November 1 to December 15 window for real and personal property, and the Property Tax page links to a lookup and payment portal.

sections.h2: How and when do you pay Maury County tax?
sections.html:
The county side runs on a longer calendar than the city side. Payment opens in early October and stays penalty-free until the final day of February, then 1.5% interest starts on March 1 and climbs monthly.

Partial payments are welcome, though interest applies to anything unpaid on March 1. A postmark counts as the payment date until the Trustee hands delinquent accounts to Chancery Court on April 1.

The Trustee lists these ways to pay:

  • Walk in at the office on Public Square.
  • Mail a check to Maury County Trustee at the same address.
  • Use the drop box outside the office after hours, with checks only.
  • Pay online by card or e-check; the vendor, not the county, takes a 2.5% fee.
  • Call 1-877-556-4502 to pay by phone.
  • Ask about monthly ACH debits that split the bill into equal installments.

sections.h2: Is 2026 a reappraisal year in Columbia, and how do you appeal?
sections.html:
It is. The Assessor's page describes a four-year cycle and calls 2026 the current reappraisal year. Values on the Assessor's records come from the market as it stood on January 1 of the last reappraisal year, with equalized improvement values added.

A taxpayer who thinks the value is unfair can go to the local board of equalization, then to the State Board. Per the state's calendar, the county board begins meeting June 1, and the State Board deadline is August 1 or 45 days after the county board mails its decision, whichever comes later. The 2026 county board stage is behind us, so a new challenge points to the next cycle.

sections.h2: What tax relief can Columbia homeowners apply for?
sections.html:
Two layers of help exist. The state program covers seniors, owners who are completely and permanently disabled, disabled veterans and their surviving spouses, and the city adds a modest credit of up to $75 a year for qualifying seniors.

To qualify for the senior or disability route, household income for the prior year must be $38,470 or less, counting you, a spouse and anyone else named on the deed. Seniors need to have reached 65 by the end of the prior year. Disabled applicants need certification from the Social Security Administration or another qualified agency. The state program is help paying local bills, and it is not a separate state tax.

Veterans with a 100% rating and their surviving spouses file Form F-16 or F-16S with Department of Veterans Affairs paperwork, available at the City Recorder's Office in City Hall. Every application is due January 20 of the current year, and the Trustee's staff will also help with the state forms.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Columbia itself?
sections.html:
Columbia has grown quickly. The Census Bureau recorded 41,690 people in 2020 and estimates 50,072 for mid-2025, a rise of 20.3% over its estimates base. A special census run for the city in 2024 reported 48,885.

The town was platted in 1808 and incorporated in 1817 on the Duck River, where the Nashville Basin ends. It bills itself as the mule capital of the world and holds Mule Day each April. Columbia State Community College has its main campus here, Maury County Public Schools teaches the city's children, and the James K. Polk Home is a regular stop for visitors.

Census QuickFacts lists these 2020 to 2024 figures:

  • Typical owner-occupied home value: $308,700.
  • Share of housing units lived in by their owners: 63.3%.
  • Median gross rent: $1,197.
  • Median household income: $63,719.
  • Households: 18,039.

sections.h2: How do you estimate a Columbia tax bill by hand?
sections.html:
The Assessor's page gives the sequence: appraised value times the ratio for the property class, then that product times the rate. A home in Tennessee's residential class uses 25%.

A house valued at the Census figure of $308,700 would carry $77,175 of assessed value. Divide by 100, then multiply by the county rate and by the city rate. Get both rates from the Trustee and the City Recorder, since the Maury County Commission and the city council set them through their budgets.

In a reappraisal year the appraisal itself moves, so set the new notice beside last year's before you assume the total will look the same.

sections.h2: How does Columbia's climate and housing age affect a sale?
sections.html:
The NOAA normals reproduced on Wikipedia show about 57 inches of rain and melted snow in a typical Columbia year, a July afternoon high near 89 degrees, and roughly an inch of snowfall. The climate is humid subtropical.

Show a buyer the tax history up front: request written balances from the Trustee and the City Recorder before listing. A county balance still open at April 1 goes to Chancery Court, so settle it before that date. Payments postmarked on time are honored up to then.

faqs.q: When is Columbia, TN city property tax due?
faqs.a: City tax is due without penalty from November 1 through December 15. Because today is November 15, 2026, there is still a month to pay for this year. After December 15, 0.5% is added through December, another 0.5% from January 1 and 1% a month from February 1.

faqs.q: When does Maury County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: March 1. County tax can be paid from the first Monday of October through the last day of February, and interest of 1.5% applies from March 1, growing monthly. Delinquent accounts go to Chancery Court on April 1.

faqs.q: Do I pay both city and county tax in Columbia?
faqs.a: Yes. The City of Columbia says anyone living within the city limits must pay both city and county property taxes. The city bills its own tax, and the Maury County Trustee bills the county portion.

faqs.q: Is there property tax relief for seniors in Columbia?
faqs.a: Yes. Seniors 65 or older with income of $38,470 or less can apply for state relief, and the city adds up to $75 a year for qualifying seniors. Applications are due January 20 of the current year.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about my Columbia home's value?
faqs.a: Call the Maury County Property Assessor at 931-375-4001 or visit 6 Public Square. Reappraisals are done every four years, and 2026 is the current reappraisal year in the county.
